prompt.context: Your client is an automobile interior plastic product manufacturing company. The client's market share is 20% and the industry's growth rate is nominal. Over the past two quarters, their profits have stagnated and the CEO is concerned. The company has only one customer and the customer continuously forces the client to price down. The company has one factory outside of Detroit and the factory is running at 70% utilization. The company manufactures 42% of the product on that factory and outsources the remaining 58%.
prompt.question: The CEO would like to improve factory utilization as well as improve profitability. Could you help develop some recommendations?

clarifying_info.q: What products does the company make?
clarifying_info.a: Two products: Plastic Rugs (mats) and Small Parts.

clarifying_info.q: What are the volumes, costs, and prices for each product?
clarifying_info.a: Internal production: Plastic Rugs — 100 tons, full cost $6, price $7; Small Parts — 40 tons, full cost $4.70, price $5. Outsourced production: Plastic Rugs — 180 tons, full cost $8, price $7; Small Parts — 80 tons, full cost $4.70, price $5.

clarifying_info.q: What is the internal factory capacity?
clarifying_info.a: The factory currently runs at 70% utilization producing 140 tons, so full capacity is 200 tons.

clarifying_info.q: Will the customer increase order quantity?
clarifying_info.a: No, the customer has no plans to increase order quantity.

clarifying_info.q: Are there differences between the two products?
clarifying_info.a: Small parts are more labor intensive to produce than mats. Mats lend more brand recognition to products than small parts. Parts produced internally have higher quality than outsourced parts. Outsourced work has lower labor cost than internal.

framework: Understand current profitability: calculate margin per product for internally produced vs. outsourced volumes
Identify which products are profitable vs. loss-making under current mix
Analyze factory capacity and determine optimal internal/external production mix to maximize profit
Quantify the profitability improvement from the optimal mix
Address broader strategic concerns beyond the immediate math (customer concentration, brand, quality, labor)

questions.prompt: Calculate the current total profit given the existing internal and outsourced production mix.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute margin per ton for each product/source combination, multiply by volume, and sum. Internal Rugs: ($7-$6)x100 = $100. Internal Small Parts: ($5-$4.70)x40 = $12. Outsourced Rugs: ($7-$8)x180 = -$180. Outsourced Small Parts: ($5-$4.70)x80 = $24. Total = $100+$12-$180+$24 = -$44. The company is currently unprofitable.

math.setup: Margin = (Price - Full Cost) x Quantity for each product-source combination

questions.prompt: What is the maximum internal factory capacity, and how should the client reallocate production to maximize profitability?
questions.guidance: Internal capacity = 140 tons / 0.70 = 200 tons. Since outsourced Rugs lose $1/ton while internal Rugs make $1/ton, the company should maximize internal Rug production up to capacity. Move all outsourced Rugs to internal: that requires 200 tons of internal capacity (100 existing + 180 outsourced = 280 total demand, but max capacity is 200, so fill with Rugs first). Optimal: 200 tons of Rugs internally, 0 Small Parts internally; outsource 80 tons of Rugs and all 120 tons of Small Parts... Actually, total Rug demand = 100+180 = 280. Internal capacity = 200. Fill internal with Rugs: 200 tons. Remaining Rug demand outsourced = 80 tons. Small Parts all outsourced = 120 tons (40+80). Recalculated profit: Internal Rugs ($1)x200=$200; Outsourced Rugs (-$1)x80=-$80; Outsourced Small Parts ($0.30)x120=$36. Total = $200-$80+$36 = $156. Improvement = $156-(-$44) = $200.

math.setup: Internal capacity = current volume / utilization rate = 140 / 0.70 = 200 tons. Reallocate: maximize high-margin internal Rugs first, push remaining demand to outsource.
steps: Total Rug demand = 100 + 180 = 280 tons; total Small Parts demand = 40 + 80 = 120 tons
Fill internal capacity with Rugs (higher internal margin): 200 tons of Rugs internally

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the immediate production mix optimization, what other concerns should the client address?

categories.name: Customer concentration risk
ideas: Single customer creates extreme pricing power on buyer side
Client should explore diversifying its customer base
Dependence makes the company vulnerable to losing all revenue

categories.name: Brand and product positioning
ideas: Mats provide more brand recognition than small parts
Prioritizing mat production aligns with brand strategy
Shifting mix toward mats could support premium pricing over time

categories.name: Labor relations
ideas: Shifting work internally may affect outsourced workforce relationships
Union or contractor agreements may constrain flexibility
Internal labor costs vs. outsourced labor costs need ongoing monitoring

categories.name: Quality control
ideas: Internal production yields higher quality than outsourced
Customer satisfaction may improve with more internal production
Quality differentiation could be a negotiating lever with the customer

categories.name: Future demand and capacity planning
ideas: If customer volumes grow, internal capacity may need to expand
If volumes decline, fixed costs of internal factory increase per-unit
Scenario planning for demand fluctuations is important

recommendation: Immediately reallocate production to maximize internal factory capacity for Plastic Rugs, bringing internal Rug output to 200 tons (full capacity) and outsourcing remaining demand
This shift improves profitability from -$44 to +$156, a $200 improvement, while simultaneously raising factory utilization to 100%
risks: Continued pricing pressure from the single customer could erode margins even after the mix improvement
Full dependence on one customer remains a structural vulnerability
Outsourced Rug production still loses money ($1/ton); if volumes increase, losses on outsourced portion grow
next_steps: Negotiate with the current customer to stabilize or increase pricing, leveraging quality advantage of internal production
Explore acquiring additional customers to reduce concentration risk and absorb any remaining outsourced production at better economics
Evaluate capital investment to expand internal capacity if demand justifies it, eliminating all outsourced Rug production
